title: For families experiencing homelessness, sometimes what's missing isn't the will to get back on their feet - it's the support to get there. That's the idea behind Family Promise Salt Lake, where Executive Director Brian Diggs sees firsthand how much a community can change a family's path.
text:
Brian Diggs, Executive Director of Family Promise Salt Lake, believes that homelessness often stems from a lack of community support rather than financial failure alone. The organization provides a unique program where families not only receive shelter but also engage in case management to develop a path toward stability and independence.
For families experiencing homelessness, sometimes what’s missing isn’t the will to get back on their feet — it’s the support to get there. For families experiencing homelessness, sometimes what’s missing isn’t the will to get back on their feet — it’s the support to get there.
That’s the idea behind Family Promise Salt Lake, where Executive Director Brian Diggs sees firsthand how much a community can change a family’s path.
“We believe that families don’t necessarily run out of money and become homeless. They run out of community,” Diggs said. He remembers one single mother with a two-month-old baby who was walking between the shelter, daycare and work.
Then someone in the community stepped up and gifted her a car. It’s the kind of support Family Promise works to build for families experiencing homelessness. For 30 years, Family Promise has helped families find stability. But Diggs says the organization is more than a traditional shelter.
“We’re very clear with our families when we interview them that this is a program, not just a traditional shelter,” he said. Families receive a place to stay, but they also work with the organization on a plan to move forward.
“In traditional shelter, you can stay without case management,” Diggs said. “We are a program that offers that same bed. But we do require our families to follow that program. ” The goal is to help families eventually have a place of their own, and Diggs says seeing that progress makes the difficult days worth it.
“This is not the easiest work, believe it or not,” he said. “It’s tough work, day to day. But it’s those kinds of stories — this young woman getting the car or that family moving into a place of their own — that make this work worth it. ” So, today, we wanted to give some of that support back to Diggs and Family Promise with a surprise gift from Mountain America Credit Union.
